decisions.reason: The LHD loaders sit at the core of the firm's underground mining expertise and share engineering, parts and service with the rest of the fleet, so holding this option costs little while its long-cycle mining demand is still unfolding.

The underground dump trucks complement the loaders in a combined mining fleet offering, and the missing website observations reveal nothing negative about their value, so keeping the low-cost option open remains rational.

The construction site dumper was only mentioned in passing and fits the core business less closely, but it uses shared vehicle know-how and there is no evidence of failure, so it stays as a cheap option.

The inclined furniture lift line was presented on its own page, which signals commitment, and its simple design and service needs make it inexpensive to keep while demand for removal and craft equipment is still being tested.
The building material lifts share components with the furniture lifts and serve steady construction demand, so the low holding cost justifies keeping the option open.
The truck-mounted lift is a more capital-intensive variant whose value is still uncertain, but it draws on the same lift platform and nothing indicates poor results, so management keeps it for now.
